correctness.rationale: The real-linear kernel follows exactly from the degree-two angular Fourier coefficients at five fifth-root samples and two distinct radial nodes. Its generator has two positive and one negative eigenvalues and full rank. Rank-one PSD perturbations cannot compensate a negative two-dimensional subspace for negative parameter. For positive parameter, a strictly positive 2x2 principal block and the explicitly derived Schur complement yield exactly 0<t<=tau(q) with the claimed endpoint ranks. The off-circle sample evaluates to (u^2-r^2)(u^2-s^2), proving injectivity and scalar minimality. The Gaussian-STFT identity follows by a convergent Gaussian Fourier transform; the numerical checker directly verifies the measurement ranks, positivity boundaries, normalized counterexample and independent quadrature. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The familiar qualitative rank-one uniqueness is insufficient to know whether convex PSD reconstruction can return spurious covariances. The exact coefficient inequality splits every source into unique versus a line segment of higher-rank competitors, proves the sharp boundary and rank transition, and identifies one new scalar datum as necessary and sufficient to remove all Hermitian ambiguity. The explicit trace-one counterexample has mutually orthogonal supports and trace distance one. This is a complete natural finite-dimensional tomography classification, not arbitrary numeric enumeration or a routine parameter rescaling; it does not claim general noisy stability or a larger-degree classification.
